changes.statement: dct:description The DALICC deontic dependency graph with default rules for what a licence does not say, under the law of Brazil: moral rights the law declares inalienable, integration of a program with another, which the software law allows, and mining, for which the list of limitations has no entry. The graph is complete: it holds the axioms and the adopted rule of the core graph beside its own rules, and it is built from the core graph and a difference file. Each rule names its legal basis and says in plain words what it does. The rules are proposals until the association's legal reviewer adopts them. Nothing in this graph is legal advice.

changes.reason: Every published graph is now complete, a jurisdiction can remove a core axiom or replace a core rule, and every rule explains itself in plain words. licensedata/dependencygraph/differences/dg_br.ttl is now the source of truth and scripts/build_dependency_graphs.py writes this graph from it and the core graph; the rules keep their outcomes, territories and bases.

The explanations of the rules were reviewed against the statutes they cite; two were corrected: the rule on reverse engineering says that article 6(IV) of Lei 9.609/1998 allows only the integration of a program for the user's own use, keeping its essential characteristics and where technically indispensable, and is therefore an approximation, with no exception for decompiling; and the mining rule says that only a mining act that reproduces a protected work needs a licence, unless a narrower limitation of article 46 applies. The adopted endorsement rule of the core graph cites its basis, says that only a use suggesting endorsement is refused, and names who adopted it. Follows core graph version 3.
